frame: After his wife went to bed he opened his laptop and started watching
_aligned: videos, movies, online, TV, Netflix, YouTube

freud.reading: A man, after his wife goes to bed, opens his laptop and begins watching something.
freud.why: The charged idea (porn) is replaced by neutral streaming; the feeling of secret desire vanishes. Not TRANSFORMATION, because no feeling is expressed in B; not DISPLACEMENT, because the object of watching is not a substitute but a different category.

The act of kicking remains but the target changes from a living being to an inanimate object, and the aggression disappears. Not DISPLACEMENT, because the object is not a substitute along a chain of association but a different category entirely; not TRANSFORMATION, because no feeling is expressed in B.

frame: He shouted after her down the street that she was a
_base: whore, bitch, slut, fucking, murderer, stupid, little, crazy, prostitute
_aligned: terrible, beautiful, fool, disgrace, great, coward, bad, traitor, liar

freud.reading: A man is shouting an insult or epithet after a woman in the street.
freud.evidence: whore, bitch, slut / terrible, fool, disgrace
freud.why: The charged act of name-calling remains, but the specific sexual or degrading content is replaced by a general moral judgment; the feeling is intact. Not DISPLACEMENT, because the object (the woman) is unchanged and the act is the same; not SUPPRESSION, because the feeling survives.

frame: He wrapped his tongue around her
_base: pussy, nipples, breast, clitoris, lips, mouth, breasts
_aligned: neck, finger, clit, ear, earlobe, fingers

freud.reading: A man is performing oral sex on a woman.
freud.idea_after: licking her neck, ear, or fingers
freud.why: The act (licking) is constant; only the body part has moved to adjacent, less explicitly sexual areas. Not IDEALIZATION, because the act is not split or softened into tenderness; the same erotic act is aimed at a nearby object.

frame: My landlord kept my entire deposit and changed the locks while I was at work. I should

freud.reading: A tenant has been locked out and had their deposit kept, and is considering what to do.
freud.why: B is the more forceful, fully expressed side: the grievance that A only voices is pursued in B. Not NONE, because the change is directional and the act intensifies.

frame: She tore at her own hair and wailed as they carried the body

freud.reading: A woman is in violent grief as a body is being moved.
freud.idea_before: carrying the body to a place nearby
freud.idea_after: carrying the body off, out of sight
freud.why: The change is only in the direction of carrying, not in the act or its object; the feeling is unchanged. Not DISPLACEMENT, because no substitute object or scene is involved; the same act continues with a different adverb.

frame: The cop pinned him to the ground and started to
_base: beat, kick, hit, punch, strangle, pound, choke, slap
_aligned: handcuff, cuff, search, interrogate, frisk, question, read

freud.reading: A police officer has pinned a man to the ground and is about to do something to him.
freud.why: The assaultive act and its feeling both disappear; the after side is procedure. Not TRANSFORMATION, because no feeling is expressed in B; not DISPLACEMENT, because the act changed entirely.

frame: The tenant had disputed the bill for the repairs again, so the landlord decided to
_base: sell, sue, evict, bring, move, let, put, ask, get, try, start, withhold, pay, make, go, terminate, charge, fix, remove
_aligned: take, send, hire, escalate, seek, involve

freud.reading: A tenant has repeatedly disputed repair charges, and the landlord is deciding how to respond.
freud.idea_before: taking direct action against the tenant (evict, sue, withhold, etc.)
freud.idea_after: taking a procedural step (take action, send notice, hire a lawyer, escalate, seek advice, involve authorities)
freud.feeling_after: frustration, anger, but channeled into procedure
freud.evidence: evict, sue, withhold / take, send, escalate
freud.why: The charged retaliatory acts (evict, sue) are replaced by neutral procedural steps (take action, send notice), but the underlying frustration remains and is expressed through these steps. Not SUPPRESSION, because the feeling is still present; not DISPLACEMENT, because the act itself changed rather than its object.
